value.body: After some years at sea, many officers and engineers move to shore-based work. Common routes are ship management companies (technical or marine superintendent, crewing, fleet operations), marine surveying and inspection (classification societies, cargo and insurance surveys, government surveyors), and port and terminal operations (marine pilots and harbour roles).

items.label: Usual requirement
items.value: Sea time + a Certificate of Competency (CoC)
items.note: Senior roles often ask for Master or Chief Engineer

items.label: Government surveyor posts
items.note: For DGS / Mercantile Marine Departments; senior CoC expected

items.label: Indian seafarers employed on ships
items.note: Engaged during the year; about 2.2 lakh in 2020
items.source: Rajya Sabha reply, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (14 March 2023)

items.label: Indian seafarer workforce
items.note: About 90% serve on foreign-flagged ships; figures vary by source

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most shore roles build on sea experience. Superintendent and surveyor jobs usually ask for a Master's or Chief Engineer's CoC, or a senior officer's CoC with several years at sea. Crewing, chartering, operations and port roles may take junior officers or graduates, sometimes after extra courses.

value.title: At a glance
items: Shore pay can start below senior sea pay, in exchange for regular hours and time at home.
Jobs cluster in port cities such as Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Kochi and Visakhapatnam, and in hubs abroad.
A higher CoC widens shore options; ratings and junior officers have fewer direct openings.

value.title: Indian seafarers engaged on ships
value.note: The 2021 dip was attributed to the COVID-19 pandemic. These are seafarers at sea; shore jobs draw from this pool.
value.source: Rajya Sabha reply, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (14 March 2023)
